propositions: BindingStore is a 799-line module that owns byte persistence, lifecycle policy, recovery, and peer-state delegation, creating maintenance and safety complexity with no cohesive internal ownership structure.
Production code mutates inner entry dictionaries returned by shallow all_bindings() query, violating encapsulation and creating data consistency risks.

The module must be refactored into three internal owners (repository/unit-of-work, lifecycle policy, recovery) behind a unified public facade while preserving all existing serialization, unknown-field, and compatibility behavior.

Retirement completion requires a durable tombstone as authoritative intent, with removal only when tombstone, forward, and reverse identities all agree; automatic liveness observations must never resurrect a tombstoned identity.
Recovery operations must run after staleness validation but before remote issue observation to prevent interleaving of new liveness evidence with completion of interrupted retirements.
Load, check, dry-run, preview, selection, and filtered operations must not perform any recovery writes; only explicit validated write-bearing operations may repair interrupted retirements.
